articles.title: From cameras to speakers, UGREEN just launched a whole smart home ecosystem in one go
articles.summary: TL;DR UGREEN’s big smart home push involves the launch of a smart speaker, photo frame, and multiple cameras. The outdoor cameras are designed to work perfectly with the company’s new local-AI smart home hubs, and include both wired and solar-powered options. A smart speaker also makes it easy to connect with the company’s Uliya digital assistant. In addition to its pricey new smart home hubs , UGREEN is getting its smart home ambitions up to speed with a slate of its own hardware, including a speaker, photo frame, and trio of cameras. We’re looking at one indoor camera and two mountable outdoor cameras: the SynCare Indoor Cam ID500 Pro, SynCare PoE CAM OD600 Pro, and SynCare Battery Cam OD800 Pro. All three offer an 8MP, 4K main camera.

articles.title: Digital Wellbeing could soon give you a weekly reality check
articles.summary: TL;DR Google is working on a Weekly wrap feature for Digital Wellbeing that could proactively recap your phone usage. Gemini Nano could turn your weekly screen-time data into personalized, contextual insights instead of just showing raw numbers. The feature is still in development, and there’s no guarantee Google will release it to users. Google’s Digital Wellbeing app is the place you’d go to know exactly how much time you’re spending on your phone . The catch, however, is that it’s largely a passive tool that you need to manually open and dig through. The tool doesn’t take a proactive approach, though that might soon change. Digital Wellbeing could soon add a new Weekly wrap feature that, exactly as it sounds, would give you a weekly recap of your phone usage.

articles.title: Confused about which VPN is right, US senator asks the NSA for guidance
articles.summary: A prominent US senator is asking the National Security Agency to provide guidance to the general public on best practices for using virtual private networks to secure their communications from spying by foreign adversaries. VPNs funnel all of a user’s Internet traffic through an encrypted connection to a remote server. The design provides strong assurances that no one between the user and the server can read the encrypted contents. VPNs also allow users to hide their IP addresses from the destination servers they communicate with. While US agencies have previously recommended use of VPNs, none have given recommendations on which ones provide adequate protection. It's all in the nuances There are a host of limitations that can undo many of the protections users may think their VPN provides

articles.title: Supreme Court urged to let states regulate sports bets on prediction markets
articles.summary: New Jersey yesterday asked the Supreme Court to rule on whether states can regulate sports betting on prediction markets such as Kalshi. “Companies like Kalshi claim to offer legal sports betting in all 50 states, but they refuse to follow the gambling laws of any state," New Jersey Attorney General Jennifer Davenport said in a press release announcing the lawsuit. In April, the US Court of Appeals for the 3rd Circuit ruled that New Jersey cannot regulate sports bets on prediction markets. The court determined that sports-related event contracts meet the legal definition of "swaps," giving the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) exclusive jurisdiction.
